title: DAPPREMO — Data Protection and Privacy Relationships Model
description:
DAPPREMO (Data Protection and Privacy Relationships Model) is a relational model for the personal data protection and privacy domains, based on set theory. Each area of activity is treated as a domain, that is, a set whose objects are its rules, activities and processes. The personal data protection domain is composed of legal rules together with non-homogeneous objects such as ethical principles, which belong to it by virtue of a shared characteristic property. The model describes the dynamic, multi-dimensional relations between such domains and between the individual objects they contain, and supports the identification of objects that are relevant to a case but habitually overlooked.

This repository hosts the canonical, versioned specification of the model, which restates it in normative form: numbered definitions, relation types, explicit assumptions, and a clear separation between normative and informative sections.

The model was created by Nicola Fabiano in 2020. Its most recent peer-reviewed version is the chapter published in the proceedings of the 11th Annual Privacy Forum (APF 2023).
